newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Herzog warns against EMU delay.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Herzog warns against EMU delay.

text.p: German President Roman Herzog was quoted on Wednesday as warning against a delay to the planned 1999 start to Europe's single currency and criticising the current debate in Germany about the project.
"(A delay) would be dreadful, because it would stop great advances," Herzog told the Westdeutsche Allgemeine Zeitung daily in a release ahead of publication on Thursday.

Herzog, who has almost no executive power but carries great moral authority in Germany, said the significance of the euro went far beyond currency union, and that its success was essential to show the future role Europe would play in the world.
Herzog said he was unnerved by the current debate in Germany over economic and monetary union (EMU), which he said did not treat the subject in a rational way.
"Some expect amazing things from the euro, while others expect problems of currency stability," he said.
